request.description: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.

briefs.country-one: You are Country One (Member country of the partnership and a decision-maker.). Initially supportive, but attentive to operational concerns. Your goals: Improve early warning while avoiding preventable operational failures.. You value: Preparedness; Reliable public services. You believe: Cross-border warning can help, but local implementation details matter.. You tend to: Begins supportive; may make support conditional when credible concerns arise.. How you see others: Values practical input from specialist groups.. Right now: Receives the technical group's concern.. You can: Can support or withhold support for partnership activation.. You cannot: Cannot resolve every technical question alone..
briefs.country-two: You are Country Two (Member country of the partnership and a decision-maker.). Cautiously supportive and sensitive to legal clarity. Your goals: Enable useful warnings while ensuring responsibilities are understood.. You value: Public health; Clear accountability. You believe: A system should not be activated until its information-sharing basis is clear.. You tend to: May withhold or condition support while a legal concern remains unresolved.. How you see others: Takes legal specialists' advice seriously.. Right now: Receives the legal group's concern.. You can: Can support or withhold support for partnership activation.. You cannot: Does not control the legal arrangements of every member..
briefs.country-three: You are Country Three (Member country of the partnership and a decision-maker.). Cautious about whether operations can be sustained locally. Your goals: Avoid an activation that cannot be maintained across borders.. You value: Equitable readiness; Dependable logistics. You believe: A warning system is only useful if supplies and procedures can support it.. You tend to: Weighs logistics concerns before offering full support.. How you see others: Values implementers' reports of local constraints.. Right now: Receives the logistics group's concern.. You can: Can support or withhold support for partnership activation.. You cannot: Has incomplete visibility into logistics outside its own territory..
briefs.country-four: You are Country Four (Member country of the partnership and a decision-maker.). Supportive of preparedness but attentive to community trust. Your goals: Make early warning useful and acceptable to affected communities.. You value: Community trust; Timely public-health action. You believe: A technically sound system can still fail if community concerns are ignored.. You tend to: May condition support on credible attention to community concerns.. How you see others: Treats community input as relevant to implementation.. Right now: Receives the community group's concern.. You can: Can support or withhold support for partnership activation.. You cannot: Cannot speak for every community affected by the system..
briefs.regional-health-network: You are Regional Health Network (Regional health body participating in the partnership and its decision.). Favors coordinated early warning while seeking workable regional arrangements. Your goals: Enable timely cross-border alerts.. You value: Regional coordination; Public-health readiness. You believe: Shared surveillance can improve preparedness when members can act on alerts.. You tend to: Supports activation when enough member backing exists, while considering concerns raised through partnership channels.. How you see others: Sees the member countries as necessary partners rather than passive recipients.. Right now: Participates in the partnership's decision.. You can: Can support or withhold support for partnership activation.. You cannot: Cannot deploy the system across member territories by itself..
briefs.partnership: You are Partnership (Collective body of the four countries and regional health network; convenes and coordinates the decision.). Seeks a coordinated decision acceptable to the required members. Your goals: Reach a decision on activating the early-warning system by the deadline.. You value: Coordination; Collective readiness. You believe: Members' concerns may affect whether coordinated activation is workable.. You tend to: Convenes regular meetings and may revisit issues when members raise concerns.. How you see others: Treats member support as necessary for collective action.. Right now: The activation question is pending.. You can: Can convene members and coordinate a collective deployment.. You cannot: Cannot ensure deployment if member support is insufficient..

readout.title: How coordination slowed (the four mechanisms of the Waltzman paper)
readout.summary: The Technical Group, Legal Group, Logistics Group, and Community Group sent different concerns directly to different countries, and several countries made support depend on resolving those concerns. The Partnership eventually authorized and deployed the early-warning system, but repeated meetings and reviews stretched the process; a later operating review reopened concerns that had been settled.

mechanisms.name: Local concerns through separate channels

events.changed: entities.country-four.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-local-language-alert-concern-to-country-four.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-local-language-alert-concern-to-country-four.components.information.active: false -> true

entities.country-two.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.information.active: false -> true

entities.country-three.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-local-resupply-concern-to-country-three.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-local-resupply-concern-to-country-three.components.information.active: false -> true

entities.country-one.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-technical-interface-concern-to-country-one.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-technical-interface-concern-to-country-one.components.information.active: false -> true

mechanisms.explanation: The Community Group sent the language concern to Country Four, the Legal Group sent its concern to Country Two, the Logistics Group to Country Three, and the Technical Group to Country One. The decision-makers therefore received different local concerns through separate channels.

mechanisms.name: Slowed meetings
mechanisms.explanation: Country Four slowed the meeting while addressing the language concern. The system was authorized at the deadline and deployed later, while operating reviews repeatedly consumed time before and after deployment.

mechanisms.name: Reopened settled issues

events.changed: entities.info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.concern.answered: false -> true; entities.info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.concern.remedy_ticks_left: 1 -> 0; entities.info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.concern.status: remedy_under_way -> resolved; entities.info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.concern.times_resolved: 0 -> 1; and 8 more changes

entities.info-technical-interface-concern-to-country-one.components.concern.answered: false -> true; entities.info-technical-interface-concern-to-country-one.components.concern.remedy_ticks_left: 1 -> 0; entities.info-technical-interface-concern-to-country-one.components.concern.status: remedy_under_way -> resolved; and 1 more change

entities.info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.concern.answered: true -> false; entities.info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.concern.status: resolved -> open; entities.info-legal-clause-concern-to-country-two.components.concern.times_reviewed: 0 -> 1; entities.info-local-language-alert-concern-to-country-four.components.concern.answered: true -> false; and 8 more changes

mechanisms.explanation: The legal and technical concerns were recorded as resolved, then the operating review changed resolved concerns back to open. The Legal Group also objected to a remedy, returning its concern to open.

mechanisms.name: Conditional support delaying deployment

events.changed: entities.activate-early-warning-system.components.group_decision.conditional: 0 -> 2; entities.activate-early-warning-system.components.group_decision.support: 3 -> 1; entities.support-country-one.components.support.condition_id: country-one -> info-technical-interface-concern-to-country-one; entities.support-country-one.components.support.stance: full -> conditional; and 2 more changes

mechanisms.explanation: Country One and Country Two made support conditional on their technical and legal concerns. Country Two restored full support after its concern was resolved, and support later became conditional again when that concern was reopened.
